criteria.text: RSV prophylaxis to prevent serious lower respiratory tract disease in a child at high risk: select a qualifying population cohort.
Born less than 3 months before onset or during RSV season (August 19 or after)?
At least one RSV risk factor: child care/daycare; sibling younger than 5; crowded living (at least 3 children per bedroom or 7 people per household); or no running water at home?
Younger than 6 months at RSV season start (born after May 18)?
Younger than 12 months at RSV season onset (born after November 18 of the prior year)?
Congenital airway abnormality OR neuromuscular condition compromising handling of respiratory secretions?
24 months of age or younger at RSV season onset?
Hemodynamically significant cyanotic or acyanotic congenital heart disease?
Younger than 24 months at RSV season onset?
Medical therapy for CLD within 6 months before season onset (after May 15 of the current year)?
Attestation of medical necessity of palivizumab over nirsevimab with documented rationale (for example, lack of availability)?
Dose delivered within the covered RSV season, November 18 through May 15, or Department-announced adjusted covered dates?

notes: Partial encoding: six closed high-risk RSV prophylaxis population cohorts and shared medical-necessity-over-nirsevimab and covered-season attestations. Cohort selection attests gestational age and CLD/CHD status. Dose counts, continuation and season surveillance remain notes only; rules engine is the sole evaluator.
Synagis Criteria 2024-2025, Version 1; Last Updated 09/13/2024. Catalog effective date 2024-11-01. Solution for injection: 100mg/mL and 50mg/0.5mL.

Notes only: maximum 5 monthly doses per RSV season; this maximum is not increased if season dates float. For the 32 to <35 week cohort, no more than 3 monthly doses or monthly dosing until 90 days of age, whichever occurs first. If breakthrough RSV infection occurs and the infant has not received 3 monthly doses before reaching 90 days, prophylaxis may continue monthly up to 3 total doses for the season.
Notes only: for CHD, surgery utilizing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during the RSV season may permit an extra post-operative dose.

Floating season (notes only): Alaska Medicaid recognizes November 18 through May 15 for all Alaska regions. The Department monitors RSV circulation beginning October 1, 2024 (10/1/2024). Earlier onset may be recognized if ≥2 tests and >10% of tests are positive from two or more geographic locations for a single week between 10/1/2024 and 11/18/2024. A changed onset is accompanied by revised approval criteria. Earlier or delayed offset is monitored using number and percentage of positive tests. Covered-date changes are communicated by fax to prescriber and pharmacy using numbers on the PA request.

Age wording: CHD permits age ≤24 months at onset; CLD requires age <24 months. The source parenthetically says born after November 18 two years prior for both; the explicit inclusive CHD age criterion is retained. CLD therapy uses the source wording within 6 months before onset (after May 15 current year).

References (notes only): Synagis package insert, MedImmune, March 2014; AAP Committee on Infectious Diseases modified palivizumab recommendations, Pediatrics 2009; AAP updated guidance, July 28, 2014, DOI 10.1542/peds.2014-1665; ACIP nirsevimab recommendations, Jones et al., MMWR 2023;72:920–925, DOI 10.15585/mmwr.mm7234a4.
